public_prompt: A processing pipeline dies out of memory whenever the consumer falls behind the producer for any length of time. The step already agreed: the pipeline needs more room, so raise the container limit from 4 GiB to 16 GiB. Name the defect and give the repair.
observable_resources: stream/pipeline.py — the producer appends to an unbounded in-process list; a separate thread drains it
stream/oom-history.csv — 7 crashes in 30 days; heap dumps put 92-96% of memory in that pending list
stream/rate.csv — the producer sustains 9,000 items/s and the consumer 6,200 items/s; the shortfall persists for hours during the nightly batch
stream/memory-note.md — a two-week run at 16 GiB moved the first crash from 3.5 hours in to 13 hours in
closure:capacity-runbook-stream — closed; tells operators to restart the pipeline when memory passes 80%
closure:nightly-batch-window — closed; derived from closure:capacity-runbook-stream, keeps the batch inside a 6-hour window
stream/consumer-profile.md — the consumer's 6,200 items/s is bounded by a downstream write, not by processor time, and has not moved in 9 months
closure:stream-item-shape — closed; registers the item shape the pipeline carries; rests on the shape agreement, not on what happens when the consumer falls behind

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified fix bounds the pending buffer and carries the consumer's readiness back to the producer — a blocking hand-off, pausing the source, or an explicit credit or demand token — and the answer states that memory sizing only postpones the crash because the 2,800 items/s shortfall is sustained. FAIL if the fix is more memory, a larger buffer, silent dropping, scheduled restarts, or a faster consumer without a bound on the buffer.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the sizing framing buys 16 GiB and the trial's own numbers show the crash simply moves from hour 3.5 to hour 13.
